DO NOT write any code or make edits. This is a READ-ONLY audit.

Read and audit these admin route files for bugs, missing functionality, UI/UX issues, and Shopify ecosystem violations. For each file, check:
1. Auth: `authenticate.admin(request)` at top of loader/action
2. DB scoping: every query has `where: { shop: session.shop }`
3. Error handling: try/catch in every action
4. Loading states: SkeletonPage when navigation.state !== "idle"
5. Empty states: EmptyState component when data is empty
6. Toast feedback: after every mutation
7. Polaris compliance: no raw HTML for layout
8. Functional correctness: does the logic actually work correctly?
9. UX issues: confusing flows, missing confirmations, accessibility
10. Billing: plan gating where needed

Files to audit:
- app/routes/app.widget.tsx (Widget config + live preview)
- app/routes/app.settings.tsx (Settings)
- app/routes/app.pricing.tsx (Billing/pricing)
- app/routes/app.help.tsx (Help page)

Read each file completely and report ALL issues found with file:line references.

# Audit Report — Admin Route Files

---

## app/routes/app.widget.tsx

### BUG — Action has no try/catch (lines 101–195)
The entire `action` function has no error handling. A failed `db.widgetConfig.upsert` call (Prisma error, connection drop) will throw an uncaught exception and return a 500 page instead of a usable error. The `save` and `reset` intent branches must each be wrapped in `try/catch` returning `{ error: string }`.

### BUG — Toast fires before server confirms success (lines 946)
In `handleSave`, `shopify.toast.show("Widget settings saved")` is called immediately when the form is submitted, before the `fetcher` returns. If the server action fails silently (returns `null` or an error), the toast already told the user it succeeded. Toast should only fire inside the `useEffect` that watches `fetcher.data`, as is done correctly in `app.settings.tsx`. The existing `useEffect` at lines 878–887 only clears `isDirty` on success but never shows a toast — the toast is misplaced in the submit handler.

### BUG — Reset action has no try/catch and no error toast path (lines 155–192)
Same as the save action. `db.widgetConfig.upsert` in the `reset` branch is bare. If it fails, the user already sees local state wiped (because `handleResetConfirm` resets all state before the server returns) with no error feedback.

### BUG — `customCss` saved even for non-Ultimate plans (lines 141)
The action reads and saves `customCss` unconditionally. There is no server-side plan check. A free-plan user who crafts a raw POST request can save arbitrary CSS. The action must call `getShopSubscription` and gate `customCss` behind `limits.customCss`, nulling it out otherwise.

### BUG — `blockCartOnInvalid` / `blockCheckoutInCart` not gated on server (lines 137–138)
Same issue as above — these Pro-only flags are saved without any server-side plan check.

### BUG — `position`, `primaryColor`, etc. not gated on server for Free plan (lines 109–141)
All widget customization fields should be gated behind `limits.widgetFullCustom` on the server. Currently the UI disables inputs but the server accepts all values regardless of plan tier.

### BUG — `c` cast hides TypeScript type information (line 831)
`const c = config as unknown as WidgetConfig;` is a double-cast escape hatch. The Prisma return type of `db.widgetConfig.findUnique` includes nullable fields (e.g. `customCss: string | null`, `codAvailable`, `returnPolicy`) that are not in the local `WidgetConfig` type. This suppresses legitimate TS errors. The loader return type and the `WidgetConfig` interface should match the Prisma schema exactly.

### BUG — No skeleton / loading state (missing)
The page has no `SkeletonPage` when navigation is loading. There is no check on `useNavigation().state`. Other pages in this codebase appear to follow the same omission, but it violates the CLAUDE.md rule (item 4 of the audit checklist).

### UX — Discard resets to stale loader data (lines 1005–1032)
`handleDiscard` reads from `c`, which is the loader snapshot at page load time. If a save succeeds and the user then changes fields again and clicks Discard, the values revert to the pre-save state — not the last-saved state — because React Router does not re-initialize the `useState` values after a `fetcher` save (the loader does not re-run). The discard function should reference a `savedState` ref that is updated after each successful save, not the original loader snapshot.

### UX — "Reset to Defaults" is available without `isDirty` guard (lines 1049–1052)
The Reset button appears in `secondaryActions` unconditionally. This means a user with default settings can click "Reset to Defaults" and trigger a DB write and metafield sync for no reason. The button should either be disabled or hidden when the current state already matches defaults.

### UX — `position` change is silently ignored on Free plan (lines 1073–1091)
`PositionTile` correctly sets `disabled={!limits.widgetFullCustom}` but the `onSelect` handler is still invoked when `disabled=true` is clicked by keyboard — only `onClick` is guarded. The `onKeyDown` handler at line 791 calls `onSelect(value)` when `!disabled`, which is correct, but `onClick` at line 789 has `!disabled && onSelect(value)` — this is actually fine. However, even if the user manages to call `onSelect`, `setIsDirty(true)` will fire and `isDirty` will be true. The server will still accept the value (see the server-side gating bug above). Together, these two bugs let a Free plan user save position changes.

### UX — `syncConfigMetafield` errors are silently swallowed (lines 96–98)
The catch block is empty with only a comment. If the metafield sync fails (e.g. wrong scope, API version issue), the stored DB config and the metafield config will silently diverge. The error should at minimum be logged (`console.error`) so it appears in server logs.

### POLARIS — Raw `<input type="color">` used for color pickers (lines 1129–1283)
Multiple raw HTML `<input type="color">` elements are used for color picking. This violates the CLAUDE.md Polaris-only UI rule. Polaris does not have a native color picker, so this may be an intentional workaround, but the raw `<div>` wrappers around them and the inline `style` attributes are also non-Polaris layout. At minimum the label/layout structure should use Polaris `FormLayout` or `BlockStack`/`Text` and the styling should use Polaris tokens.

### POLARIS — `PositionTile` uses raw `<div role="button">` (lines 785–821)
A custom `<div role="button">` is used instead of a Polaris component. Given Polaris v13 does not have a tile/card-select component, this is understandable, but the inline `style` object uses hardcoded pixel values and CSS custom properties (e.g., `var(--p-color-border-emphasis)`) mixed — and Polaris CSS custom property names change between versions. All layout and spacing should use Polaris tokens via the `style` system or Box/BlockStack.

## app/routes/app.settings.tsx

### BUG — `ShopSettings` model may not exist in DB at query time, but Prisma `findUnique` does not create it (lines 40–41)
The loader calls `db.shopSettings.findUnique({ where: { shop } })` and then uses `?? "block"` defaults. This is safe for reading. However, the action uses `db.shopSettings.upsert` which is correct. No bug here on its own, but see the next issue.

### BUG — No try/catch in loader (lines 33–50)
The loader has no `try/catch`. A DB connection failure or Prisma error throws unhandled, bypassing the `ErrorBoundary` for unexpected errors. Loaders should catch DB errors and either return a safe fallback or re-throw for the boundary.

### BUG — Email validation is done client-side only by HTML `type="email"` (lines 315–322)
The action at lines 77–86 performs no server-side email format validation. It accepts any string as `notificationEmail`. A malformed email string is persisted to the DB. The action should validate the email format with a regex or similar before upserting.

### UX — Error display uses `<Text tone="critical">` instead of `Banner` (lines 272–278, 308–314)
Inline errors for both `behaviorFetcher` and `notificationFetcher` render as plain `<Text tone="critical">`. CLAUDE.md says to use `Banner` for persistent alerts. Errors from server actions are persistent (they stay until the next action) so they should be `<Banner tone="critical">`.

### UX — "Data Management" buttons navigate to other pages, not actual export/delete actions (lines 405–415)
The "Export Zip Codes" button in the Data Management card navigates to `/app/zip-codes` instead of triggering an actual CSV export. This is misleading — a user clicking "Export Zip Codes" in a Settings page expects a file download, not navigation to the list page. Either rename the button to "Manage Zip Codes" or implement actual export.

### UX — No loading skeleton (missing)
No `SkeletonPage` is used when navigation state is loading. Violates CLAUDE.md item 4.

### UX — No `Toast` for error cases (lines 89–91)
The action catch block returns `{ error: "..." }` and the UI displays it inline via `<Text tone="critical">`, but there is no toast for the error. For save failures, a toast saying "Failed to save" is expected per CLAUDE.md item 6.

### FUNCTIONAL — `handleSaveAll` fires multiple concurrent fetcher submits (lines 152–165)
`behaviorFetcher.submit` and `notificationFetcher.submit` are called back-to-back in the same synchronous call. React Router does allow concurrent fetchers, but both go to the same action route. If both change, two concurrent POST requests hit the same action, and the second might overwrite or conflict with the first depending on DB transaction ordering. The pattern is technically functional but fragile — a single submit with both intents would be safer.

## app/routes/app.pricing.tsx

### BUG — `test-set-plan` intent is exposed in production (lines 178–191)
The "Set Plan Manually" UI block (lines 552–577) and the `test-set-plan` action intent are permanently visible and functional in the production-facing page with no environment check. Any merchant can bypass Shopify billing by directly posting `intent=test-set-plan&tier=ultimate` to this route and get Ultimate features for free. This must be gated: either remove it entirely from production or wrap the entire block behind `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` on both the action handler and the JSX rendering.

### BUG — No try/catch in loader (lines 124–129)
The loader calls `getShopSubscription(shop)` with no error handling. A DB failure throws unhandled.

### BUG — `billing.cancel` is called before checking if `sub.shopifySubscriptionId` is truthy, but cancel proceeds to `cancelShopSubscription` regardless (lines 193–211)
The logic at line 196 checks `if (sub.shopifySubscriptionId)` before calling `billing.cancel` — that part is fine. However, `cancelShopSubscription(shop)` at line 203 runs unconditionally even if `billing.cancel` threw an error that was caught silently. Since the `catch` block at line 208 only returns an error message without preventing the DB update, a partial state can occur: if `billing.cancel` fails (Shopify side), the DB is still reverted to free, leaving the subscription in an inconsistent state where Shopify still bills the merchant but the app treats them as free.

### BUG — Duplicate error display (lines 443–448 and 488–490)
There are two separate error banner renders for `actionError`. One is rendered as its own `Layout.Section` at lines 443–448, and another is rendered inside the `BlockStack` at lines 488–490. Both will appear simultaneously when an error occurs, showing the same error message twice.

### BUG — `setLoadingPlan(null)` clears loading state before toast fires (lines 394–399)
In the `useEffect`, `if (!isFetching) setLoadingPlan(null)` runs unconditionally on every state change when `isFetching` is false. This is in the same effect that reads `data.message`. The dependency `isFetching` means the effect fires when fetching ends — but `setLoadingPlan(null)` will also fire on initial render before any fetch occurs, which is harmless but sloppy. More critically, once `isFetching` becomes false after a `test-set-plan` action that returns `{ success: true, message: "..." }`, the toast fires AND `loadingPlan` is cleared in the same effect run, which is fine — but the `loadingPlan` state drives the individual `PlanCard` `loading` prop. If `loadingPlan` is cleared before the card re-renders, the loading spinner flickers off before the user sees it. This is a minor visual race condition.

### UX — No loading skeleton (missing)
No `SkeletonPage` used when navigation state is loading.

### UX — Annual toggle does not update the "Set Plan Manually" block (lines 552–577)
The manual plan setter always sets `billingInterval: "monthly"` (line 187) regardless of the `isAnnual` toggle state. If a user is testing annual billing, they must know to ignore the toggle for the manual setter.

### UX — Cancel confirmation modal warns about features that may not apply (lines 601–630)
The modal at line 606 says "Unlimited zip codes — limited to 20" regardless of the user's current plan. If the user is on Starter (limit 500, not unlimited), this text is factually incorrect.

### UX — "Start 7-day free trial" CTA shown on every non-current paid plan (lines 272–281)
The `buttonContent` logic shows "Start 7-day free trial" for any paid plan when the current user is on Free. But if the user has previously had a trial (e.g. they cancelled), Shopify's billing API may not allow a second trial. There is no check against trial history, so the button may show "Start 7-day free trial" but the Shopify billing confirmation page will charge immediately. This requires checking `subscription.trialEndsAt` or Shopify's trial eligibility.

## app/routes/app.help.tsx

### FUNCTIONAL — Getting Started list renders items as unlinked strings (lines 35–40, 92–101)
The `gettingStartedItems` array contains strings like "How to add ZIP codes" and "Setting up delivery rules" that are rendered as `<List.Item>` text with no links or navigation. A help page should link these to the actual feature pages (e.g. clicking "How to add ZIP codes" should navigate to `/app/zip-codes`). Currently the list provides no actionable value.

### FUNCTIONAL — FAQ answer for Free plan zip limit is incorrect (lines 44–47)
The FAQ says "Free: 25 allowed zones" but `plans.ts` line 38 sets `maxZipCodes: 20` for the Free tier. This is a factual inconsistency that will confuse merchants.

### FUNCTIONAL — Documentation and Feature Requests links point to placeholder domains (lines 183–199)
`https://docs.zipcodechecker.app` and `https://feedback.zipcodechecker.app` are used. If these domains do not exist and resolve to 404 or an unrelated site, clicking them from a live store will send merchants to broken links. These should either be real working URLs or replaced with `mailto:` or the actual support channel.

### UX — No loading skeleton (missing)
No `SkeletonPage` used when navigation state is loading.

### UX — `Layout.Section variant="oneHalf"` is used for Support Hours but the next section is full-width (lines 135, 170)
`Layout.Section variant="oneHalf"` renders the Support Hours card at 50% width. However, there is no second `variant="oneHalf"` section beside it to fill the row. The resulting layout will show Support Hours at half-width with a blank column next to it, which looks like a broken layout. Either use a full-width section or pair it with another half-width section.

### UX — No action (no `action` export, no fetcher forms) — correct, but support contact has no in-app form
The help page is purely static. The "Email Support" button opens an external `mailto:` link. Within a Shopify embedded app, `mailto:` links typically open in the parent browser tab and may not function properly inside the admin iframe on all browsers. An in-app contact form (fetcher + action writing to a support ticket or sending an email) would be more reliable.

## Cross-Cutting Issues (all four files)

### No `SkeletonPage` / navigation loading state in any file
None of the four files import or use `SkeletonPage`, `SkeletonBodyText`, or `SkeletonDisplayText`. CLAUDE.md item 4 requires a loading state when `useNavigation().state !== "idle"`. This is missing across the board.

### Loader error handling absent in all files
None of the loaders (`app.widget.tsx:34`, `app.settings.tsx:33`, `app.pricing.tsx:124`, `app.help.tsx:23`) wrap their DB/auth calls in `try/catch`. The `ErrorBoundary` will catch unhandled throws but the UX is an error page rather than a graceful degradation.

### `PLAN_LIMITS` used with `as PlanTier` casts instead of strict typing
In `app.widget.tsx:833` and `app.settings.tsx:103`, the subscription `planTier` is cast with `as PlanTier` before indexing `PLAN_LIMITS`. Since `getShopSubscription` already returns `planTier: PlanTier` (strictly typed in `billing.server.ts`), these casts are redundant but mask any future type widening.
